title: Kargil political groups hold shutdown over winter election schedule
seoTitle: Kargil shutdown over winter election timing

tea.why: Political and social groups in Kargil are protesting the decision to hold hill council elections during the region's harsh winter months.
tea.want: The protesters want the administration to reschedule the elections to avoid the winter season.
tea.changed: Nov 10: The Ladakh administration announced that hill council elections will proceed on December 4 despite the ongoing shutdown in Kargil.

summary: On November 10, 2026, political and social groups in Kargil observed a shutdown to protest the Ladakh administration's decision to hold hill council elections on December 4. Organisers, including the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), argued that the timing is unsuitable due to the region's severe winter conditions, noting that a significant portion of the population may be away during this period. The Ladakh administration, led by Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra, defended the schedule, stating that the elections are necessary for timely budget preparation and that polling stations will be equipped with heating facilities. While the administration described the polls as a democratic milestone, local groups criticised the move as an example of bureaucratic overreach. The shutdown in Kargil coincided with the official announcement of the election schedule for the newly expanded hill councils.
demands: Reschedule elections to avoid winter months
response: Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra stated that the elections are necessary for budget planning and confirmed that deputy commissioners will provide heaters and other facilities at polling stations to assist voters.

updates.text: Kargil observed a shutdown to protest the scheduling of hill council elections during the winter season.
